conventions: The ASV reaches the bare objects of this chapter's verbs of proclamation through a supplied preposition — יֹאמֵרוּ → 'shall speak of' (vv. 6, 11), יְרַנֵּנוּ → 'shall sing of' (v. 7), יְדַבֵּרוּ → 'talk of' (v. 11), אָשִׂיחָה → 'Of ... will I meditate' (v. 5). Every such word is given to the verb's unit under rule 44 and never to the object noun under rule 33, and a second occurrence written over a coordinated member joins that same discontinuous unit under rule 25, which is why both 'Of's of v. 5 are the verb's. Where a preposition morpheme does stand before the object, rule 11's priority governs instead and that morpheme takes the word: לְכָל־חַי → 'of every living thing' (v. 16) puts the 'of' on the לְ.

דּוֹר is read twice, by what the ASV writes. In v. 4 דּוֹר לְדוֹר → 'One generation ... to another' spends an English word on each of the three morphemes: the supplied 'One' joins the first noun as the determiner of its nominal expression under rule 15, the לְ takes 'to' discontinuously under rule 25, and the second, repeated דּוֹר takes the correlative 'another' as its own rendering, no אַחֵר standing in the phrase for it — marking that noun unrepresented and 'another' added would leave a written lexical noun holding nothing against rule 2. In v. 13 בְּכָל־דּוֹר וָדֹר → 'throughout all generations' is rule 22's distributive repetition instead: the first occurrence takes 'generations', the waw and the repeated occurrence are unrepresented, and the determiner slot before the noun is filled by the written כֹּל, which takes 'all'.

A construct chain the ASV renders attributively writes no relational word between its two nouns, so rule 19 has nothing to place there and an 'of' standing before the whole phrase is the phrase-level word rule 33 gives to the noun opening it: גְדָל־חָסֶד → 'of great lovingkindness' (v. 8) puts 'of great' on גְדָל and leaves חֶסֶד its bare 'lovingkindness'. Where the ASV does write the relation between the two nouns, rule 19 governs as usual — אֶרֶךְ אַפַּיִם → 'Slow to anger' (v. 8) puts 'to anger' on the rectum. In v. 7 the two readings meet in one phrase: זֵכֶר רַב־טוּבְךָ → 'the memory of thy great goodness' gives the 'of' to רַב as the rectum of זֵכֶר under rule 19, while the inner רַב־טוּב chain is attributive and writes no second relation for טוּב.
report: Read all 21 candidate lemma groups and the full verse dump end to end. No cross-verse split found: every multi-treatment bucket traces to a difference the ASV itself wrote, not to one construction analysed two ways. patches is empty.

אָמַר (v6 vs v11) is the closest call and is licensed. v6 supplies the lexical noun 'men', which rule 17 marks added; v11 writes the pronoun 'They', which rule 17 gives to the verb. Both verses then place the verb's supplied 'of' the same way under rule 44.

לְ and בְּ alternate between rendered and unrepresented exactly with whether the ASV spends a word on the relation — v14 'upholdeth all' and 'raiseth up all' bare against v18 'unto all' and 'To all'; v2 'Every day' bare against v13 'throughout' and v17 'in'. Rule 40's condition rather than the lemma decides each, and each is decided the same way.

דּוֹר is two constructions, not two analyses: v4 דּוֹר לְדוֹר spends an English word on each of three morphemes, so rule 2 splits it, while v13 דּוֹר וָדֹר writes one noun and no connective, which is rule 22's distributive repetition. Rule 22's own second limit already separates them.

Head differences inside expanded substantives are rule 31's subtraction test working, not drift: 'mighty acts' (vv. 4, 12) and 'terrible acts' (v6) head on the modifier because the ASV never writes 'acts' alone for גְּבוּרָה or נוֹרָאוֹת, while 'tender mercies' (v9) heads on 'mercies', which is רַחֲמִים's own word under rule 31's tie-breaker.

The candidate table is keyed by source lemma and cannot see added units, so I checked the supplied English verse by verse instead. Three added units (v1 'A Psalm of', v6 'men', v13 'endureth'), and the chapter holds rules 20 and 34's boundary consistently: supplied copulas join their predicates (vv. 3, 8, 9, 17, 18), a supplied lexical verb is added (v13), and no supplied word is folded into a licensing morpheme in one verse and marked added in another.

All 11 BSB disagreements are documented convention differences — recast prepositions under rule 40 (vv. 2, 3, 14 twice, 15), the vocative article under rule 36 (v1), the object markers under rule 16 (vv. 15, 20), the resumptive suffix of אֲסַפְּרֶנָּה and the דּוֹר וָדֹר repetition under rule 22 (vv. 6, 13). None is a genuine error and no accepted edge was touched.

Conventions: the report's 22 repeated notes are almost all restatements of binding rules and are not logged. Three are real chapter-wide judgments and are recorded: the supplied 'of' on verbs of proclamation, the two readings of דּוֹר, and where the 'of' of an attributively rendered construct chain goes.

Promotions and amendments: none. The two cases that tempted one — the correlative 'another' carried by a repeated noun with no אַחֵר present (v4), and the אֵין חֵקֶר fusion to 'unsearchable' (v3) — already follow from rule 22's second limit and from rules 23 and 30, and the packet carried no דּוֹר corpus rows to support widening rule 15.
